not_covered: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled a strategic direction for frontier reasoning models characterized by the native integration of vision into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, as well as incorporating native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) directly into the training process [Source: ev-1].

The release highlighted a new approach to compute efficiency through "budget forcing," which utilizes a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive dynamic compute, allowing harder questions to require longer thinking times [Source: ev-1].
Strategically, the launch was an effort by OpenAI to defend the frontier of reasoning capabilities against competitors DeepSeek and Anthropic while GPT-5 had not yet shipped [Source: ev-1].

By offering o3 at $10 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, and o4-mini at $1.10 per million input tokens and 4.40 dollars per million output tokens [Source: ev-1], OpenAI reframed frontier capability as tool-using reasoning available at commodity prices [Source: ev-1].

This direction is further evidenced by o3 setting a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark with approximately 87.5% accuracy on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute levels, reaching or exceeding the ~85% human baseline [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled a strategic shift in frontier reasoning models toward integrating vision natively into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, as well as incorporating native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) directly into the training process [Source: ev-1].

The release also highlighted a new approach to compute efficiency through "budget forcing," which utilizes a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive dynamic compute, allowing harder questions to require longer thinking times [Source: ev-1].
